hypotheses.statement: High isotropy / weak coherent structure favors particle trajectory history over material threads.
hypotheses.conditions: Validated in homogeneous isotropic decaying turbulence across seeds 101-104.

hypotheses.statement: Strong organized shear / coherent deformation favors connected material thread history.
hypotheses.conditions: Validated in Taylor-Green and Kelvin-Helmholtz shear layer flows.

hypotheses.statement: Thread advantage correlates with local velocity-gradient topology.
hypotheses.conditions: Local velocity gradient invariants (strain eigenvalues, Q, R, rotation/strain ratio) provide genuine predictive signal.

hypotheses.statement: An adaptive selector can outperform the globally best fixed Lagrangian representation.
hypotheses.conditions: Adaptive model A1 dynamically switches between particle and thread representations using local flow invariants.

hypotheses.statement: Adaptive Lagrangian information can add predictive value beyond reduced instantaneous Eulerian physics.
hypotheses.conditions: Convex combination of physics and topology-gated Lagrangian representation outperforms both pure physics and ungated concatenations.

hypotheses.statement: The adaptive selector generalizes to unseen flow realizations.
hypotheses.conditions: All scaling, gating training, and hyperparameter selection strictly confined to training folds in LOFO.

hypotheses.statement: The adaptive selector generalizes to completely unseen flow families.
hypotheses.conditions: Cross-family transfer strongly succeeds for isotropic and shear layer regimes, but is marginal for highly periodic Taylor-Green states.
